Skip to main content WorktreeSecret Broker DemoInstallPrivacy Local CLI · v0.1.0 Lease secrets to one worktree process For developers running coding agents, each worktree gets only approved development variables. Try it with sample dataOpens an isolated recorded CLI run. Only approved variables enter the child.Receipts list names, never values.Production labels are denied by default. Only approved variables reach the named worktree process. Sample names-only receiptThe receipt shows names, never valuesThe recording uses the demo’s two bundled names. wsb demo · isolated sample00:00:01 $ wsb demo Demo — sample data, nothing is saved Temporary worktree: /tmp/wsb-demo-4821 Approved: DATABASE_URL, NPM_TOKEN Lease: 15 minutes → sample check ✓ child received 2 approved variable names Receipt demo-1787913600 worktree: /tmp/wsb-demo-4821 names: DATABASE_URL, NPM_TOKEN started: 1787913600 expires: 1787914500 outcome: demo-complete revoked: 1787913601 Temporary worktree removed. How it worksRun one worktree process in three steps 01Map approved namesPoint each variable name at Keychain, Secret Service, or 1Password.DATABASE_URL → keychain://my-app/database-url 02Name the worktreeThe broker checks the Git root before starting one child process.wsb run --worktree ../agent-42 -- npm test 03Read the receiptExpiry stops the child. The receipt lists names, timing, and outcome.outcome: child-exited · names: NPM_TOKEN cargo install --git https://github.com/B-Divyesh/sf-worktree-secret-broker.git --lockedView source (external site)Copy install command A narrow toolWhat the broker does not do It does not host a vault.It does not scan repositories.It denies production-labelled entries by default.It cannot hide variables from the child that needs them.
